In short

A plant maintenance contract from Online Plants Cart puts a trained gardener on your site on a fixed schedule. Each visit covers watering, pruning, cleaning of leaves, soil health, pest and disease checks, and seasonal feeding. Contracts run monthly, quarterly or annually across Delhi, Gurugram, Noida and the wider NCR, and most include replacement of plants that fail while under our care.

What happens on a maintenance visit

A visit is not a person with a watering can. Our gardener works through a fixed routine, and the order matters, because half the job is noticing problems while they are still small.

Watering, properly

Watering to depth rather than wetting the surface, and only where the soil actually needs it. More office plants die of overwatering in Delhi NCR than of drought, which surprises almost everyone. If the top two inches are still damp, the plant is skipped that visit.

Pruning, cleaning and shaping

Dead leaves removed, growth shaped, and dust wiped off the foliage. Leaf cleaning sounds cosmetic and is not. A layer of Delhi dust measurably reduces how much light a leaf can use, and indoor plants here have very little light to spare.

Soil and feeding

Soil condition checked, topped up or replaced where it has compacted, and seasonal feeding applied. Feeding is reduced through peak summer, because a plant under heat stress cannot use it and the salts do more harm than the nutrients do good.

Pest and disease checks

Mealybug, spider mite, scale and fungal spotting are the common problems in NCR offices and gardens. Caught in the first week they are a five minute job. Caught in the sixth they are a replacement.

The visit note

Every visit ends with a short written note saying what was done and what needs watching. Clients tell us this is the part they value most, because it turns plant care from something invisible into something they can actually see happening.

Choosing a contract that fits the site

Weekly visits

Suited to offices with a large number of indoor plants, newly installed planting in its first month, and any site where nobody on the premises will touch a plant between visits.

Fortnightly visits

The most common choice for established offices. Frequent enough to catch problems, infrequent enough to keep the cost sensible.

Monthly visits

Works for homes and small gardens that already have someone doing basic watering, where our role is the skilled work rather than the daily routine.

Seasonal adjustment

Schedules are not fixed for the year. Frequency rises through May and June and eases through the cooler months, and outdoor sites move to early morning visits in summer. Watering an exposed garden at midday in a Delhi May does more harm than skipping it.

What a contract covers, and what it does not

Included

  • All scheduled visits at the agreed frequency
  • Watering, pruning, cleaning, feeding and repotting where needed
  • Pest and disease treatment
  • Replacement of plants that fail through normal causes on annual contracts
  • A written note after every visit and a named contact you can call between visits

Charged separately

  • New plants added to expand the planting rather than replace it
  • Losses from causes outside our control, such as construction dust, a burst pipe, or a plant moved into a dark store room
  • Major one time work such as re landscaping a bed or replacing all the soil in a large planter

We would rather set this out plainly at the start than have the conversation later with an invoice in hand.

Taking over plants that are already struggling

About half our maintenance clients come to us with planting that has been neglected for a while, sometimes for years. That is a normal way to start and it does not embarrass anybody.

The audit comes first

The first visit is an audit. You get an honest assessment of which plants are worth saving, which are healthy but in the wrong position and should be moved, and which are past recovering. Then a recovery plan with realistic timelines.

What to expect in the first three months

Slower progress than you want. Recovering neglected planting takes longer than starting fresh, because a stressed plant has to rebuild its root system before it can put out the growth you will actually notice. Month one looks like tidying. Month three starts to look like a garden.

Who we maintain plants for

Corporate offices and co working spaces, housing societies and RWA common areas, independent villas and apartments, hotels and restaurants, schools and hospitals, and showrooms where the planting is part of how the space presents itself.

If your plants came from us as part of an office plant rental, maintenance is already included and there is nothing further to arrange. If we built your garden through our landscaping service, a maintenance contract for the first year is the single best thing you can do to protect that investment.

Frequently asked questions

What does a plant maintenance contract cover?

Watering to the right depth rather than a daily splash, pruning and shaping, cleaning dust off leaves so they can actually photosynthesise, checking soil condition, seasonal feeding, and catching pests and disease early.

You also get a short written note after each visit saying what was done and what needs watching. It is the part clients say they value most, because it turns plant care into something you can actually see happening.

How often should office plants be watered?

Less often than most people think, and more thoroughly when you do. For typical indoor office plants in Delhi NCR, once a week in winter and twice a week through peak summer suits the majority of species.

Overwatering kills far more office plants than drought. If the top two inches of soil are still damp, the plant does not need water yet, whatever the schedule on the wall says.

What is the difference between an AMC and paying per visit?

An annual maintenance contract fixes the price, guarantees the schedule and usually includes replacement of plants that fail while we are looking after them. Per visit work costs less on any single visit and includes none of that.

Per visit suits a garden that already has a regular gardener and needs occasional expert attention. An AMC suits anywhere that has nobody responsible day to day.

How much does monthly garden maintenance cost?

It scales with area, plant count and visit frequency rather than following a fixed rate. A small office with twenty indoor plants on a fortnightly visit sits at one end. A society with lawns, hedges and seasonal beds needing twice weekly attention sits far at the other.

We quote after seeing the site, because quoting before seeing it means either overcharging you or discovering the real scope later and asking for more.

Do you replace plants that die under contract?

On annual contracts, yes, replacement is included for plants that fail through normal causes while under our care. That is the whole logic of the arrangement. If we are responsible for the health of the plant, we should carry the cost when it does not survive.

Losses from causes outside our control, such as construction dust, a burst pipe or a plant moved into a dark store room, are charged at cost.

Can you maintain plants you did not supply?

Yes, and about half our maintenance clients came to us that way. We start with an audit that tells you honestly which plants are worth saving, which are in the wrong place and should be moved, and which are already too far gone.

Expect the first two or three months to look like slow progress. Recovering a neglected planting takes longer than starting fresh.

Will the same gardener come every time?

We keep the same person on a site wherever we can, because someone who knows your plants spots a problem weeks before a stranger would. Leave and rotation mean it cannot be an absolute promise, so every site has written notes that travel with the job.

What happens to plants during peak summer in Delhi?

May and June are the hardest months here and the schedule changes to suit. Watering frequency goes up, feeding is reduced because plants under heat stress cannot use it well, exposed plants get shade netting, and pruning is kept light.

We usually move outdoor sites to early morning visits through summer. Watering at midday in a Delhi May does more harm than good.

Do you handle pest control on plants?

Yes, as part of every visit. Mealybug, spider mite, scale and fungal spotting are the common ones in NCR offices and we treat them at the first sign rather than after they have spread.

We use the mildest effective treatment first, which in an occupied office usually means a soap based spray and manual removal rather than a strong chemical.

Can we start with a one time visit before committing?

Certainly. A single audit and clean up visit is a sensible way to see how we work, and it gives you a written assessment of your plants that is useful even if you go no further with us.
